reason: Section 14.3 applies where project-site work has continued more than ninety days and 30 to 499 employees work at the site, then sets contractor establishment duties, representative composition, employer and employee designations, dissolution when the site exceeds 499 employees, and transfer of committee records.

proposedGroups.titleSuggestion: Medium-sized project-site committee triggers, composition, dissolution, and records
proposedGroups.reason: Section 14.3 applies where project-site work has continued more than ninety days and 30 to 499 employees work at the site, then sets contractor establishment duties, representative composition, employer and employee designations, dissolution when the site exceeds 499 employees, and transfer of committee records.
proposedGroups.approximateLearningGoal: Recall when a medium-sized project-site committee is required, how it is composed, and what happens when the site becomes large.

reason: Section 14.4 defines trade for the section, applies when 500 or more employees work on a project site, requires committee establishment, sets employer, employee and contractor representation, and allows committees to designate additional trades.

proposedGroups.titleSuggestion: Large project-site committee trigger, trade representation, and designated trades
proposedGroups.reason: Section 14.4 defines trade for the section, applies when 500 or more employees work on a project site, requires committee establishment, sets employer, employee and contractor representation, and allows committees to designate additional trades.
proposedGroups.approximateLearningGoal: Recall when a large project-site committee is required and how trade-based employee and employer representation works.

reason: Section 14.5 applies to project sites and sets training prerequisites for co-chairs and committee designees, exceptions for recent committee or representative service, optional training leave, Commission leave orders, and pay and benefits protection.

proposedGroups.titleSuggestion: Training eligibility, grandfathering, leave orders, and pay for project-site committee members
proposedGroups.reason: Section 14.5 applies to project sites and sets training prerequisites for co-chairs and committee designees, exceptions for recent committee or representative service, optional training leave, Commission leave orders, and pay and benefits protection.
proposedGroups.approximateLearningGoal: Recall the project-site committee training prerequisites, exceptions, leave order, pay and benefit rules.

reason: Section 15 lists committee functions across recommendations, hazard identification and control, hazard communication, education programs, complaints, records, information gathering, monitoring, inspections, investigations, and assigned duties.

proposedGroups.titleSuggestion: Functions of joint health and safety committees

evidenceText: participate in the identification and control

proposedGroups.reason: Section 15 lists committee functions across recommendations, hazard identification and control, hazard communication, education programs, complaints, records, information gathering, monitoring, inspections, investigations, and assigned duties.
proposedGroups.approximateLearningGoal: Identify the functions a joint health and safety committee may perform at the place of employment.

reason: Section 16 permits the Commission to reduce meeting frequency for low-risk employment if safety is not materially affected, and to schedule meeting times where scheduled meetings would disrupt operations.

proposedGroups.titleSuggestion: Commission changes to committee meeting frequency or timing
proposedGroups.reason: Section 16 permits the Commission to reduce meeting frequency for low-risk employment if safety is not materially affected, and to schedule meeting times where scheduled meetings would disrupt operations.
proposedGroups.approximateLearningGoal: Recall when the Commission may reduce committee meeting frequency or schedule meeting times.

reason: Section 17 excludes project sites, requires a safety policy for employers with 5 to 19 employees that may include a representative, allows the Commission to require a representative policy for high-risk or high-accident workplaces, and requires election and posting where a representative is provided.

proposedGroups.titleSuggestion: Health and safety representatives for non-project sites
proposedGroups.reason: Section 17 excludes project sites, requires a safety policy for employers with 5 to 19 employees that may include a representative, allows the Commission to require a representative policy for high-risk or high-accident workplaces, and requires election and posting where a representative is provided.
proposedGroups.approximateLearningGoal: Recall when non-project workplaces use health and safety representatives and how representatives are elected and posted.

reason: Section 17.1 has separate topics for project-site representative thresholds and designation numbers, and for tenure, applied functions, training pay and posting.

proposedGroups.titleSuggestion: Project-site representative thresholds, training prerequisite, designation timing, and numbers
proposedGroups.reason: These subsections identify project sites requiring representatives, set the training prerequisite and exception, require joint designation within two weeks of listed events, set one representative per 50 employees, and provide fallback designation rules if no agreement is reached.
proposedGroups.approximateLearningGoal: Recall when project-site health and safety representatives are required and how they are designated and counted.

proposedGroups.titleSuggestion: Project-site representative tenure, functions, training pay, leave orders, and posting
proposedGroups.reason: These subsections state when a representative remains in position, apply section 18 with modifications, protect training pay and benefits, allow Commission leave orders, and require contractor posting of representative names.
proposedGroups.approximateLearningGoal: Identify the tenure, function, training leave, pay, Commission order and posting rules for project-site health and safety representatives.

reason: Section 18 lets a health and safety representative do what a committee may do under section 15, requires regular consultation with the employer, and requires calling an officer if no agreement is reached on a health or safety matter.

proposedGroups.titleSuggestion: Functions and dispute resolution for health and safety representatives
proposedGroups.reason: Section 18 lets a health and safety representative do what a committee may do under section 15, requires regular consultation with the employer, and requires calling an officer if no agreement is reached on a health or safety matter.
proposedGroups.approximateLearningGoal: Recall the representative functions, employer consultation duty, and officer referral rule for unresolved health and safety matters.

reason: Section 19 gives an employee the right to refuse any act where the employee has reasonable grounds to believe it is likely to endanger their health or safety or another employee health or safety.

proposedGroups.titleSuggestion: Employee right to refuse dangerous work

evidenceText: may refuse to do any act

proposedGroups.reason: Section 19 gives an employee the right to refuse any act where the employee has reasonable grounds to believe it is likely to endanger their health or safety or another employee health or safety.
proposedGroups.approximateLearningGoal: Recall the threshold for an employee right to refuse dangerous work.

reason: Section 20 is a staged refusal-to-work process with supervisor investigation, committee referral, officer referral and remedial orders, plus employee availability while investigations or appeals are pending.

proposedGroups.titleSuggestion: Supervisor investigation and remedial action after an employee safety report
proposedGroups.reason: These subsections require the employee to report the concern to the supervisor, supervisor investigation in the employee presence, remedial action or recommendation if reasonable grounds exist, and advice to do the act if not.
proposedGroups.approximateLearningGoal: Recall the supervisor-stage duties after an employee reports that an act may endanger health or safety.

proposedGroups.titleSuggestion: Committee investigation and recommendation after unresolved refusal
proposedGroups.reason: These subsections require referral to a committee or officer if unresolved, committee investigation, recommended remedial action if reasonable grounds exist, and advice to do the act if they do not.
proposedGroups.approximateLearningGoal: Explain the committee-stage process when the employee safety concern is not resolved with the supervisor.

proposedGroups.titleSuggestion: Officer findings, orders, written advice, appeal link, and employee availability
proposedGroups.reason: These subsections require officer referral if the committee stage is unresolved, written officer findings, remedial orders or written advice, application of appeal-related provisions, and employee availability at a safe place while investigation or appeal is pending.
proposedGroups.approximateLearningGoal: Identify the officer-stage findings, remedial order or advice, appeal connection, and employee availability requirements after a work refusal.

reason: Section 21 states how long the right to refuse remains protected through supervisor, committee, officer and Chief Compliance Officer appeal stages, and prevents assigning another employee unless that employee is advised of the refusal, reasons and rights.

proposedGroups.titleSuggestion: Protection period for refused work and limits on assigning another employee
proposedGroups.reason: Section 21 states how long the right to refuse remains protected through supervisor, committee, officer and Chief Compliance Officer appeal stages, and prevents assigning another employee unless that employee is advised of the refusal, reasons and rights.
proposedGroups.approximateLearningGoal: Recall when an employee refusal remains protected and what an employer or supervisor must tell another employee before assigning the refused act.

reason: Section 22 permits temporary reassignment to reasonably equivalent work while a protected refusal continues, with same wages and benefits, subject to any collective agreement.

proposedGroups.titleSuggestion: Temporary reassignment during protected work refusal
proposedGroups.reason: Section 22 permits temporary reassignment to reasonably equivalent work while a protected refusal continues, with same wages and benefits, subject to any collective agreement.
proposedGroups.approximateLearningGoal: Recall when and how an employee may be reassigned during a protected work refusal and what pay and agreement limits apply.

reason: Section 23 requires the employer to pay the same wages and grant the same benefits when an employee reasonably refuses protected work and is not reassigned.

proposedGroups.titleSuggestion: Wages and benefits when a refusing employee is not reassigned

evidenceText: shall pay that employee the same wages

proposedGroups.reason: Section 23 requires the employer to pay the same wages and grant the same benefits when an employee reasonably refuses protected work and is not reassigned.
proposedGroups.approximateLearningGoal: Recall the pay and benefit rule for a protected refusal when no reassignment occurs.

reason: Section 24 prohibits employers, supervisors and unions from discriminatory action, threats, intimidation or coercion because an employee sought enforcement or complied with the Act, regulations, orders, or workplace-related Smoke-free Places Act requirements, and excludes section 22 reassignment from discriminatory action.

proposedGroups.titleSuggestion: Prohibition on discriminatory action for enforcing or complying with safety laws
proposedGroups.reason: Section 24 prohibits employers, supervisors and unions from discriminatory action, threats, intimidation or coercion because an employee sought enforcement or complied with the Act, regulations, orders, or workplace-related Smoke-free Places Act requirements, and excludes section 22 reassignment from discriminatory action.
proposedGroups.approximateLearningGoal: Identify the prohibited reprisals for safety-law enforcement or compliance and the reassignment exclusion.
